Rooms.Name: Barrow Top
Rooms.Description:
After struggling up the side of the barrow, you are eventually 
rewarded with a spectacular view over the surrounding countryside. On 
top of the Barrow is a large stone slab, carved deeply with some strange 
writing and what appears to be the symbol of the Crimson Fists, an order 
of knights, who fight for money.

There is nothing quite like a stroll in the countryside, birds singing 
and the heady scent of spring flowers. You wander aimlessly through the 
knee high grass and flowers, but your attention is drawn to the steep
barrow just to the southeast.

Rooms.Name: Inside the Barrow
Rooms.Description:
Your eyes strain to penetrate the gloom within the barrow, which is 
lit only by the light you carry with you. The air is thick with dust, 
and the whole area is covered with cobwebs. There is a faint musty smell 
of death in the air which appears to emanate from a large crypt in the 
centre of the barrow. The walls are decorated with tattered and ancient 
banners, and burnt out torches crumble in the rusted wall brackets.

Exits.Description: A narrow set of steps lead out of the barrow.
A rusted iron ladder leads down into the darkness.

Rooms.Name: Entrance to the Labyrinth
Rooms.Description:
The iron ladder ends abruptly and you are forced to drop the rest of 
the way to the ground, leaving you unable to climb back the way you 
came. You find yourself at the entrance to an amazing labyrinth with 
sweeping parapets in every direction. The narrow bridges twist and turn, 
climbing and falling as they wind their way through the impenetrable 
darkness. Looking along one of the bridges, you can just about make out 
another platform in the distance. A quick examination of one of the 
bridges brings a worrying conclusion - they are very unsafe and could 
collapse at any time. There must be a safe route through however. You 
hear maniacal laughter in the distance, echoing all around you.

Rooms.Name: End of the Labyrinth
Rooms.Description:
One final twist and you find yourself at the end of the labyrinth. 
You stand before a very solid looking citadel hewn from black granite. 
The walls are smooth as glass, the corners sharp and the buttresses 
imposing. Before you stands a huge statue of a mighty warrior standing 
proudly wearing thick protective plate armour and bearing the tattered 
banner of the Crimson Fists.

Exits.Description: A huge black gateway lies a short distance to the south.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The wide banner is a deep red colour, and in its time caused fear among 
the enemies of the Crimson Fists. In the centre of the banner, is a 
white circle as pure as snow, and within it a clenched armoured fist 
the colour of fresh blood.

Rooms.Name: The Gates to the Citadel
Rooms.Description:
The citadel gates are made from some dark metal you have never seen 
before, and looks incredibly heavy. Bolts extend from the gate into the 
black granite surround, and deep into the ground beneath your feet. In 
the centre of the gate is a slot, presumably for a key or talisman of 
some kind. No doubt the Knights of the Crimson Fist can gain entry at 
any time, but the citadel is surely impenetrable to their enemies. 
Dark sentry posts either side of the gate glare angrily at you - you 
hope they are unmanned.

Exits.Description:
You see the exit from the labyrinth behind you and feel glad you do not 
have to pass through it again.
A sentry post lies just to the east.
The immense gates hide what lies within the citadel.
A sentry post lies just to the west.

Rooms.Name: Sentry Post
Rooms.Description:
This dark tiny room is rather unpleasant, but the Crimson Fists are 
tougher than some wimpy little adventurer and would proudly stand here 
for hours on end, guarding the citadel.

Exits.Description: The Citadel gates lie to the east.

Rooms.Name: Hallway
Rooms.Description:
The inside of the citadel is even more impressive than the outside. 
The walls are decorated with tattered banners and all kinds of weapons. 
Every twenty paces a thick column rises on each side of the hallway 
high above your head, eventually curving into an arch which meets more 
than fifty feet above you. Elaborate chandeliers light the hallway, 
sending your shadow dancing across the floor.

Exits.Description: You see the citadel gates behind you.
A thick wooden door blocks your way east.
The imposing hallway continues south.

Rooms.Name: Aaron's Chambers
Rooms.Description:
The Chambers of Knight Lieutenant Sir Aaron are sparse to say the 
least. On the other side of the room there is an uncomfortable looking 
bed and a small table. Aside from a candle and a small Crimson Fists 
emblem, carved from a ruby, the table is bare. The only other thing in 
the room is a large armour tree, where Sir Aaron stores his platemail 
and weapons.

Exits.Description: The hallway lies to the west.

Rooms.Name: Hallway
Rooms.Description:
Huge banners hang on the walls either side of you, between the sturdy 
columns. You recognise the war standards of the Silver Hammers and the 
Sea Hawks among them, both renowned mercenary bands, and both destroyed 
by the Crimson Fists.

Exits.Description: The hallway continues north.
The hallway continues south.
A wooden door bars your way west.

Rooms.Name: Cindar's Room
Rooms.Description:
Knight Lieutenant Sir Cindar's room is not what you would expect 
from a civilised knight. The walls and floor have been painted in 
crimson, and the room is lit by four thigh-thick candles - one in 
each corner. Sir Cindar obviously sleeps on the floor, there is a 
small pile of blankets near the north wall. A wide table on the south 
side of the room is the only piece of furniture, also painted in 
crimson, but there is nothing on it.

Exits.Description: A large crimson painted wooden door leads east.

Rooms.Name: Stone Stairwell
Rooms.Description:
A wide stone staircase curves upwards to the second floor of the 
citadel. Wide swathes of crimson silk draped from the ceiling soften 
the appearance of the hard stone walls. A narrow staircase leads 
downwards to the citadel barracks and there is a large wooden door 
to the east.

Exits.Description: A wide hallway continues north.
A wooden door bars the way east.
A wide sweeping staircase leads up.
A narrow stairwell leads downwards.

Rooms.Name: Azig's Study
Rooms.Description:
The study of Knight Lieutenant Sir Azig is filled with books and 
tomes and scrolls, scattered over all the horizontal surfaces. A wide 
desk is the most striking item in the room, with thick carved legs 
and made from heavily polished oak. A small bed in the corner doesn't 
look large enough for a man of Sir Azig's reputation.

Exits.Description: west desc

Rooms.Name: Grand Hallway
Rooms.Description:
The hallway is more grand on the second level of the citadel. Thick 
tapestries cover the walls, depicting events in the history of the 
Crimson Fists - mainly their many bloody victories. The hallway 
continues north, and to the south, you can sense the peace of a place 
of worship. A large brass-inlaid wooden door leads east.

Exits.Description: The hallway continues north.
A brass-inlaid wooden door leads east.
An archway leads south.
A wide sweeping staircase leads downwards.

Rooms.Name: Crimson Fists Chapel
Rooms.Description:
The chapel is a place of solemn dignity and piety and you are 
overcome with a sense of calm. This is where the knights pray to 
their gods three times every day, and where apprentice knights 
spend their vigil, before they become true knights. A plush red 
carpet runs down the length of the chapel, to a knee high rail 
before the altar. The large altar holds only two thick candles 
which are always kept lit. Dark wooden pews are arranged down 
each side of the chapel, enough to seat all of the Crimson Fists 
at once.

Exits.Description: You see a grand hallway to the north.

Rooms.Name: Gravin's Room
Rooms.Description:
You are impressed with the rich furnishings in Knight Lieutenant Sir 
Gravin's room. A roaring fire burns beneath an ornately carved oak 
mantelpiece and a large war banner hangs above it. On the wall is a huge 
sword, taller than a man - a greatsword, apparently sharpened and ready 
for use.

Exits.Description: You see a wide hallway to the west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It is the war banner of the Emperor's Children, Sir Gravin slew their 
Primarch and Bannerman himself, taking the standard and winning another 
campaign for the Crimson Fists.

Rooms.Name: Grand Hallway
Rooms.Description:
As you walk down the grand hallway your feel a little 
unworthy. The thick columns are ornately carved, each in a 
different pattern. The floor too is richly decorated, a 
strange geometric arrangement of crimson, white, grey and 
black tiles. The hallway continues north, and there is a 
bronze banded oak door to the west.

Exits.Description: The hallway continues north.
The hallway continues south.
A large bronze banded oak door blocks the way west.

Rooms.Name: Stephen's Shrine
Rooms.Description:
Knight Captain Sir Stephen's room is as peaceful as a church, the 
walls are panelled with oak, which has been polished to a deep shine. A 
small alcove to the south holds a small cot, but it is clear that Sir 
Stephen spends more time in prayer than sleeping. A wide altar bears a 
single candle, held in a large candle-holder carved from some red-gold 
metal into the shape of a gauntleted fist.

Exits.Description: A large wooden doors least east.

Rooms.Name: Grand Hallway
Rooms.Description:
The wide corridor ends before a pair of huge oak double doors. The 
doors are edged with gold, and in the middle of each is an inlaid 
crimson fist, made from thousands of rubies. There is also door to the 
east, which has been coated with silver and polished to a mirror finish.

Exits.Description: You see a huge pair of gold-inlaid oak doors.
A silvered door leads east.
A grand hallway leads south.

Rooms.Name: Rowland's Apartments
Rooms.Description:
The apartments of Knight Captain Sir Rowland are incredibly richly 
appointed. A monstrous black glass mantelpiece runs the entire length 
of the north wall, and on the south side of the room is a long table, 
with ten high-backed carved chairs. A small curtained off area to the 
east holds a small bed and a few personal possessions, but does not 
appear to be used very often.

Exits.Description: A shiny silvered door leads east.

Rooms.Name: Grand Throne Room
Rooms.Description:
Upon entering the throne room you eye is immediately drawn to the 
high dais opposite you. The throne on top of the dais is ornately 
carved such that it appears to be made from hundreds of clenched 
fists, the plated gauntlets enamelled in a thousand shades of red. A 
rich crimson carpet edged in gold runs the entire length of the throne 
room and up the five shallow steps to the throne. Beside the dais are 
two more large thrones, carved from oak and trimmed in gold leaf, 
presumably for the two Knight Captains. There is no other furniture, 
you assume that any other members of the order must stand in the 
presence of their Primarch and his Captains.

Exits.Description: A wide pair of doors lead south.

Rooms.Name: Lost in the Labyrinth
Rooms.Description:
You don't get very far before the bridge begins to crumble beneath 
your feet, and it's collapse is so sudden that you have no chance to 
turn back. As you fall into the abyss, you hear the sound of laughter 
echoing around you.

Exits.Description: You can see nothing, you're dead!
You can see nothing, you're dead!
You can see nothing, you're dead!
You can see nothing, you're dead!

Rooms.Name: Basement
Rooms.Description:
You have entered the training area of the Crimson Fists, deep below 
their citadel. Narrow stone steps lead up, and just to the north this 
corridor appears to open out into a large and very noisy training hall.

Exits.Description: The basement opens out into a large training hall.
A narrow stone stair leads upwards.

Rooms.Name: Barracks
Rooms.Description:
The barracks of the second company of the Crimson Fists is not 
very tidy, the belongings of the soldiers strewn across the thirty 
two beds along with bits and pieces of armour, and many weapons. 
However, despite the apparent mess, the weapons and armours are very 
well cared for, and in excellent condition. Sir Cindar leads the 
second company, and like their Knight Lieutenant their appearance is 
unkempt, and maybe even a little savage. Their discipline and 
fighting prowess however are legendary, and they are never taken 
lightly by their foes.

Exits.Description: You can hear the clash of weapons coming from the east.

Rooms.Name: Training Hall
Rooms.Description:
The clash of shields and the ringing of swords assault your ears as 
soon as you enter the training hall of the Crimson Fists. All around you 
are unarmoured soldiers, practicing their swordplay and large racks of 
practice swords and shields. In this area the warriors are honing their 
single combat skills under the watchful eyes of Knight Sergeant Jem. The 
training hall extends further to the north, and there are barracks to 
the east and west.

Exits.Description: The training hall extends further to the north.
There appears to be a barracks area to the east.
You can make out a short corridor and at the end a set of stone steps.
There appears to be a barracks area to the west.

Rooms.Name: Barracks
Rooms.Description:
The barracks of the first company of the Crimson Fists has a raw feel 
to it, a tension that you can almost taste as you enter. The first 
company lead by Knight Lieutenant Sir Aaron are sometimes referred to 
as the Young Bloods, since they are the newest recruits. Like all new 
soldiers they are always extremely keen to prove their skills, sometimes 
leading to a lapse in discipline, but their savagery is unequalled 
within the Order.

Exits.Description: The training hall lies to the west.

Rooms.Name: Barracks
Rooms.Description:
The fourth company of the Crimson Fists is the most experienced, and 
consists entirely of veteran fighters. They have fought in many 
campaigns under the leadership of Sir Gravin, and some of them even 
recall the time when Sir Rowland lead them, and Gravin was just another 
one of their company. The beds lining the walls are made with military 
precision, and this is the only barracks hall containing a captured 
enemy war banner - the standard of the Iron Claws.

Exits.Description: The practice halls lie to the east.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The banner shows gloved hand with razor sharp claws on a field of forest 
green. The banner was captured at a siege as a result of the great bravery 
and skill of the fourth company, under the leadership of the then Knight 
Lieutenant Sir Rowland.

Rooms.Name: Training Hall
Rooms.Description:
Knights at this end of the training hall are drilling in formations, 
learning the discipline that will bring the Crimson Fists further glory. 
Knight Sergeant Gilbert barks orders at the small groups of sweating 
knights, always pushing them harder, forcing them to improve. The 
training hall continues further south, and there are barracks to the 
east and west.

Exits.Description: To the east you see a barracks.
The training hall continues south.
To the west you see a barracks.

Rooms.Name: Barracks
Rooms.Description:
The third company is sometimes known as the stalwart company, their 
bravery and devotion is without question. They are experienced troops 
are generally take few losses under the shrewd leadership of Knight 
Lieutenant Sir Azig.

Exits.Description: The training hall lies to the west.

Mobs.Name: knight lieutenant sir aaron crimson
Mobs.LongDescription: #yA tall young knight in crimson plate says 'Hey! Who are you?'#N
Mobs.Description:
Knight Lieutenant Sir Aaron spends his time in this chamber, when 
he is not training in the basement - drilling his men, and practicing 
with sword and lance. Sir Aaron is the youngest of the Crimson Fist 
officers, having risen through the ranks due to his skill and intense 
loyalty towards the chapter. He commands the first company of the 
Crimson Fists - known as the Young Bloods.

Mobs.Name: knight sergeant gilbert crimson
Mobs.LongDescription: Knight Sergeant Gilbert stands around barking orders.
Mobs.Description: #RKnight Sergeant Gilbert yells, 'WHAT ARE YOU LOOKING AT! MOVE IT!'#N

Mobs.Name: knight sergeant jem crimson
Mobs.LongDescription: A powerful looking Knight Sergeant glares at you.
Mobs.Description:
Knight Sergeant Jem is in charge of training the Crimson Fist soldiers 
in the use of all civilised weapons. He is a master with them all, but 
he is best with a longsword, or a flail. Jem is very powerfully built, 
glaring about him at the drilling soldiers, occasionally shouting a few 
words of encouragement.

Mobs.Name: knight lieutenant sir cindar crimson
Mobs.LongDescription: A wild looking Knight paces furiously up and down.
Mobs.Description:
Knight Lieutenant Sir Cindar has a barely contained savagery to him. To 
the casual observer he is extremely scruffy, his hair is long and hangs 
loosely halfway down his back. A closer inspection however shows that 
his armour is well oiled and his sword is very sharp. You think if would 
be best not to antagonise him.

Mobs.Name: knight captain sir rowland crimson
Mobs.LongDescription: Knight Captain Sir Rowland regards you suspiciously from across the room.
Mobs.Description:
One of the older knights in the order, Sir Rowland has risen on the tide 
of his own skill and dedication to be second in command of the Crimson 
Fists. Although he is now one of the older Knights, he has lost none of 
his speed and skill, which is now tempered with the wisdom of an older 
man.

Mobs.Name: knight HUGE lieutenant sir gravin crimson
Mobs.LongDescription: A HUGE knight in crimson armour turns to stare at you as you enter the room.
Mobs.Description:
Knight Lieutenant Sir Gravin must be the largest knight you have ever seen, 
standing more than a foot taller than any of the other knights in the 
citadel. As if his height were not intimidating enough, he is built as wide 
as a barn door, and has an angry looking scar running down the right hand 
side of his face. You doubted the stories that he had slain the bannerman 
and primarch of the Emperor's Children single handed - looking at him you 
wonder that he didn't kill the entire army.

Mobs.Name: knight captain sir stephen crimson bannerman
Mobs.LongDescription: A wise looking Knight Captain waits patiently for you to introduce yourself.
Mobs.Description:
Knight Captain Sir Stephen is the bannerman of the Crimson Fists. When the 
Order rides into battle, he carries their standard before them, giving them 
courage to face their foes. At one time Sir Stephen was a priest, and he 
still spends a great deal of time in prayer. As you might expect from a 
bannerman he is very solidly build, and looks like he doesn't put up with 
any nonsense.

Mobs.Name: knight lieutenant sir azig crimson
Mobs.LongDescription: A wiry looking knight in crimson armour scrutinises an old book.
Mobs.Description:
Knight Lieutenant Sir Azig doesn't look like the campaigning type, being 
slightly built and wearing a scratched pair of spectacles as he reads. Sir 
Azig is something of a scholar and spends all his spare time reading old 
books and scrolls. Never fear however - he can handle a sword as well as 
any of his fellow knights, and he is unsurpassed with the lance.

Mobs.Name: primarch morgan crimson fist knight
Mobs.LongDescription:
The supreme commander of the Crimson Fists, Primarch Morgan, looks down on 
you from his throne.
Mobs.Description:
Primarch Morgan sits impassively on his throne, gazing down on you with a 
calm expression on his face. He is a well built handsome man, with wide 
shoulders and the sure movements of an accomplished fighting man.

Mobs.Name: chaplain crimson order fist
Mobs.LongDescription: A pious man serves as chaplain to the Crimson Fist.
Mobs.Description:
The Chaplain is a portly fellow, almost unable to reach round his impressive 
girth, or count his chins. As well as seeing to the spiritual well being of 
the young knights, he has been known to crack a few heads.

Mobs.Name: ghost apparition crimson
Mobs.LongDescription: A crimson apparition floats before you.
Mobs.Description:
You can see through him, but you notice that the claws on the end of his 
arms look very solid.

Mobs.Name: bat red reddish
Mobs.LongDescription: A vicious looking bat swoops down on you from the darkness.
Mobs.Description:
He looks like a fairly normal bat, except for the reddish tint to his fur, 
and the malevolent glow in his eyes.

Mobs.Name: servant pale
Mobs.LongDescription: A pale servant hurries about his business.
Mobs.Description:
Doesn't look like he gets out much, probably too busy seeing to the needs 
of his masters.

Mobs.Name: soldier training crimson clad
Mobs.LongDescription: A young soldier works hard, practicing his fighting skills.
Mobs.Description:
He looks exhausted, but one glance at the stern Knight Sergeant is 
all he needs to discover those hidden reserves of energy. Besides - he 
wouldn't dare let his company down.

Mobs.Name: knight crimson fist
Mobs.LongDescription: A knight in crimson plate stands guard here.
Mobs.Description: He looks like he knows how to handle himself, better not mess with him.

Mobs.Name: stone chapterhouse guardian crimson
Mobs.LongDescription: #GA reddish stone guardian blocks the gate to the citadel.#N
Mobs.Description:
A large statue in the shape of a man blocks your progress. It's very 
detailed, and appears to be clutching a small crimson amulet.

Mobs.Name: knight crimson fist
Mobs.LongDescription: A knight in crimson plate wanders around the citadel.
Mobs.Description: He looks like he knows how to handle himself, better not mess with him.

Mobs.Name: ghoul crimson
Mobs.LongDescription: A hideous crimson ghoul pounces on you.
Mobs.Description:
He smells like an old corpse, and his clawed hands grasp hungrily for you
throat. Time to make an escape perhaps?

Objects.Name: amulet crimson fist
Objects.Description: You notice a small crimson amulet in the shape of a gauntleted fist.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The amulet is intricately carved, and enamelled in deep crimson. Some 
slight scratches along the edges of the tiny fist suggest that maybe 
it has a special use, other than for ornament.

Objects.Name: platemail crimson
Objects.Description: A pure crimson platemail looks very sturdy.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Its made of thick plates of the finest steel, enamelled the colour of 
blood. The crimson enamel appears to glow in the dim light, perhaps 
this platemail is magical?

Objects.Name: mailshirt crimson
Objects.Description: A mailshirt made from crimson links glitters like diamonds.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
You cannot work out what metal the mailshirt is made from. The links 
are finely crafted from some reddish metal, which appears to glow 
crimson in the poor light.

Objects.Name: gauntlets crimson pair plated
Objects.Description: You see a pair of crimson gauntlets, gleaming like fresh blood.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The gauntlets are cleverly constructed from small plates of enamelled 
steel, so that they resemble the armoured plates of a lobster. The 
thick enamel appears to glow.

Objects.Name: backplate crimson
Objects.Description: You notice a thick protective backplate, enamelled in crimson.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The backplate is a thick slab of solid steel the colour of blood.

Objects.Name: legplates crimson
Objects.Description: A pair of crimson legplates lie in a heap on the ground.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The legplates are ingeniously constructed from thick plates of enamelled 
steel, with strange shaped sections of even thicker plate to protect the 
vulnerable knee joint.

Objects.Name: footplates crimson pair
Objects.Description: A pair of crimson footplates stand to attention.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Overlapping scales of crimson steel make the footplates excellent 
protective footwear, although unfortunately cumbersome to wear.

Objects.Name: helmet crimson
Objects.Description: An ornate crimson helmet stares at you from across the room.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The helmet is made from enamelled steel, edged in gold. Narrow eye 
slits give you a poor view of the outside world, but at least you 
are well protected.

Objects.Name: crimson fist war banner
Objects.ShortDescription: the war banner of the Crimson Fists
Objects.Description: A tall war banner flaps gently in the breeze.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The is the war standard carried into battle by Knight Captain Sir 
Stephen, Bannerman of the Crimson Fists. In battle victory can be 
balanced on a knife edge, the fickle heart of men deciding the 
outcome. The banner is a focus of courage for all the Crimson Fist 
Knights, and so long as it stands, they will fight on.

Objects.Name: crimson armplates
Objects.Description: A pair of sturdy crimson armplates have been left here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
They are cleverly jointed at the elbow so as to allow maximum 
protection without impeding movement. The thick steel plating is 
enamelled a deep crimson - the same shade as fresh blood.

Objects.Name: crimson fist pendant
Objects.Description: A small pendant in the shape of a gauntleted fist has been placed here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It seems to be a tiny crimson gem, carved in the shape of a gauntleted 
fist attached to a delicate gold chain.

Objects.Name: crimson fist primarch signet ring
Objects.Description: You notice a large gold signet ring with a crimson emblem.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The signet belongs to the Primarch of the Crimson fists. Its made of a 
thick band of gold, and set in the face is a ruby carved in the shape 
of a clenched fist.

Objects.Name: crimson fist mace
Objects.Description: A huge crimson mace stands in the corner, daring you to pick it up.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
This HUGE crimson mace is shaped like a gauntleted fist, and is the same 
colour as fresh blood. Only the strongest hand could ever lift it.

Objects.Name: hammer war chaplains crimson fist
Objects.Description: A vicious looking war hammer looks ready for a fight.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The hammer has a large silver-steel head and a long leather bound 
handle. On one side of the head is a small emblem of the Crimson 
Fists.

Objects.Name: ruby emblem crimson fist
Objects.Description: A tiny ruby glitters on the floor.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Its carved into the shape of a crimson fist, perhaps it is a memento 
of past glories, and loyal comrades.

Objects.Name: shield crimson painted practice wooden
Objects.Description: This battered wooden shield has been painted a garish crimson colour.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It looks very well used - the paint is chipped and scarred. However it 
still seems sturdy enough to grant you protection from your enemies.

Objects.Name: sword training plain practice blunted
Objects.Description: A plain iron sword has been purposely blunted and placed on the ground.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Its very blunt, and unlikely to harm anyone save by shear brute strength.

Objects.Name: greatsword gravins engraved
Objects.Description: A huge greatsword hangs on iron hooks on one wall.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Its so long and heavy that its virtually unusable with any great skill. 
These swords were once very popular among knights who would simply swing 
the sword around, hitting anything that came into range. The greatsword 
is deeply engraved with magical runes, but the leather grip is beginning 
to dry out, suggesting that this sword is no longer in regular use.

Objects.Name: platemail crimson
Objects.Description: A pure crimson platemail looks very sturdy.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Its made of thick plates of the finest steel, enamelled the colour of 
blood. The crimson enamel appears to glow in the dim light.

Objects.Name: gauntlets crimson pair plated
Objects.Description: You see a pair of crimson gauntlets, gleaming like fresh blood.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The gauntlets are cleverly constructed from small plates of enamelled 
steel, so that they resemble the armoured plates of a lobster.

Objects.Name: backplate crimson
Objects.Description: You notice a thick protective backplate, enamelled in crimson.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The backplate is a thick slab of solid steel the colour of blood.

Objects.Name: legplates crimson
Objects.Description: A pair of crimson legplates lie in a heap on the ground.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The legplates are ingeniously constructed from thick plates of enamelled 
steel, with strange shaped sections of even thicker plate to protect the 
vulnerable knee joint.

Objects.Name: helmet crimson
Objects.Description: An ornate crimson helmet stares at you from across the room.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The helmet is made from enamelled steel, edged in gold. Narrow eye 
slits give you a poor view of the outside world, but at least you 
are well protected.

Objects.Name: crimson armplates
Objects.Description: A pair of sturdy crimson armplates have been left here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
They are cleverly jointed at the elbow so as to allow maximum 
protection without impeding movement. The thick steel plating is 
enamelled a deep crimson - the same shade as fresh blood.

Objects.Name: footplates crimson pair
Objects.Description: A pair of crimson footplates stand to attention.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Overlapping scales of crimson steel make the footplates excellent 
protective footwear, although unfortunately cumbersome to wear.
